messages.subject: Re: Shapefile map in place of the default OSM map?
messages.subject_clean: Shapefile map in place of the default OSM map?
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

I'm also new to Deducer, and incredibly relieved to find a less-intimidating way to use R.  I think I have a somewhat similar question about Deducer Spatial.  I've been able to load point, line, and polygon shapefiles with no problem, but some of the layers I was hoping to work with are raster data rather than feature data.  Is there any way to load ARC GRID, ARC ASCII, or .bil format files using Deducer Spatial?  I've seen some references that say I can use the R packages raster and rgdal to deal with these files, but I'm having trouble just getting them loaded.  Is this something Deducer can help with, or do I need to keep looking?  In either case, thanks so much for making the R learning curve a little less steep!

-Beth

On Wednesday, August 22, 2012 10:07:53 PM UTC-7, Ian wrote:
> Hum, I'm not sure exactly what you are getting at. You can plot shape
> files on top of the raster map, but there is no way to remove the
> raster image from the spatial plot builder.
>
>
> ian
>
> On Mon, Aug 20, 2012 at 8:03 PM, tgraybam <tgra...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Hi!
> >
> > I am new to Deducer and just trying to figure out DeducerSpatial. (The whole
> > setup is terrific.)
> >
> > Is it possible to load a shapefile into spatial plot builder in place of the
> > default map? And then build the rest of the plot on top of that? In
> > particular, I was wondering if I could use something like this:
> >
> > http://www.naturalearthdata.com/downloads/50m-cultural-vectors/50m-populated-places/
> >
> > Any advice?
> >
> > Thanks!
> >
> > -- Tony
> >

NOAWT=1 R CMD INSTALL ...

or from within R

Sys.setenv(NOAWT=1)
install.packages(...)

ian

messages.subject: Sharing a common R process between JGR/Deducer and RStudio?
messages.subject_clean: Sharing a common R process between JGR/Deducer and RStudio?
messages.body_plain:
Hello group,

I just learned how to run Deducer without GUI from Dr Fellows. It's very useful for me since I mainly use R on ESS and RStudio, but do benefit from Deducer's sophisticated functions.

Little demo
http://rpubs.com/kaz_yos/deducer

Also I was wondering if it is possible to "share" a common R process between two environments, so that I can do data manipulation on the ESS (or RStudio) side, and then descriptive statistics on the dataset just created on the Deducer side (two systems accessing the same R process). That way I can utilize the best part of both systems.  I tried googling, but could not come up with a good answer.

Thank you.

Kazuki Yoshida

RPubs: http://www.rpubs.com/kaz_yos/
SlideShare: http://www.slideshare.net/kaz_yos

messages.subject: Re: creating a submenu
messages.body_plain:
Not in the command line menu system or the windows GUI. Just add them
to the command line menu ( deducer() ) without putting them in a sub
menu, and attach them to the GUI with jgr.addSubMenu.

messages.subject: Re: creating a submenu
messages.body_plain:
If you are just looking to add menu items to JGR, then (as you noted)
jgr.addSubMenu is what you want. I was referring to the textual menu
system you get by typing deducer(), and the (somewhat limited)
bindings to the standard GUI that comes with R on windows.

ian
